meta.titulo: {marca}: your story, in a deck of cards
meta.descripcion: Upload your photos and get a card game at home where you put memories in order by date. For couples and families.

nav.prototipoDetalle: This is a prototype for the partners: payments are test payments and photos never leave your device.

inicio.heroAntetitulo: A card game made with your photos
inicio.heroTitulo: Your story, in a deck of cards.
inicio.heroTexto: Upload your photos, we read the dates and send you a game where you put memories in order. Was the trip to Menorca before or after your first dinner at home?
inicio.abanicoAlt: Three sample cards fanned out: one with the photo and the question, another with the date 14 August 2019.

1.texto: Drop a folder or pick from your gallery. The date comes from the photo or the file name; you only check the ones without one.

2.texto: Frame each photo, add a line if you like, and choose the style, the colour and a dedication for the cover.

3.texto: You receive a printed deck with its box and instructions that fold down to the size of a card.

inicio.cartasTexto: On the front, the photo and the question: when was it? On the back, the answer: the year in big type and a 12-month strip that marks the month. If you only know the year of a photo, that works too.
inicio.cartasPrecision: Day, month or just the year: each card carries the date you know.
inicio.modosTitulo: So the deck maker doesn’t always win
inicio.modosTexto: Whoever makes the deck knows the dates. That’s why the game comes with ways to play where that helps instead of spoiling it.
inicio.mecanicasTexto: They’re printed in the corner slot or as special cards. Turn them on or off with one tap.
inicio.preciosTexto: Pick a pack, which is the minimum to play. If you have more photos, add them 10 at a time.
inicio.packIncluye: Box, cover card with dedication, instructions and shipping in Spain

privacidad.1: In this prototype, photos never leave your device: dates are read right here.
privacidad.2: When real orders open, they’ll be stored on servers in the European Union, encrypted and private.
privacidad.3: We delete photos and print files 60 days after shipping.
privacidad.4: No third-party analytics on your images. We never use them for anything else.

1.p: How long does it take to make a deck?
1.r: About 15 minutes for 40 photos: most already carry their date and you only check the doubtful ones.

2.p: What if I don’t know the exact date of a photo?
2.r: Set just the month or just the year. In the game, a year-only card fits anywhere in that year.

3.p: What if the deck maker already knows every date?
3.r: They can play as the Memory Keeper, play as a team with everyone else, or play with a handicap. See “How to play”.

4.r: Standard poker size, 63 × 88 mm, with rounded corners.

5.r: The site is in Spanish and English, and the deck can be in either: months, card texts and instructions.

carta.enBlancoFoto: Stick a photo or draw here
carta.portadaReverso: To play, see the instructions in the box.
carta.cajaTexto: A game for putting your memories in order. Place each card before or after the ones on the table, then flip it over: did you get it right?

retos.1: Act out how you met. Everyone else guesses the year.
retos.2: Hum that summer’s song. If someone gets it, draw one card fewer.
retos.3: Say three words that sum up this year.
retos.4: Tell a memory that isn’t on any card.
retos.5: Who took this photo? Get it right and play again.
retos.6: Place a card from your hand without looking. If it fits, it stays.
retos.7: Pick someone: swap one card with them.
retos.8: Recreate the pose from the last card played.
retos.9: Name a place from the deck within 5 seconds.
retos.10: Everyone points at the most nostalgic person. They draw a card.
retos.11: Put the cards in your hand in order out loud, without looking.
retos.12: Toast: say why this memory deserves a star.

juego.intro: A game of putting memories in order. Each card has the photo on the front and the date on the back. The winner is the first to place all their cards correctly on the memory line.
juego.componentesTexto: The cards with your photos, a cover card, the wild cards and blank cards (if you chose them) and this leaflet.
juego.preparacionTexto: Shuffle and deal 4 cards to each player (3 if there are more than 5 of you), photo side up, without looking at the date. Place one card in the middle, date side up: it starts the memory line.
juego.turnoTexto: Pick a card from your hand and place it on the memory line: before, after or between two cards. Flip it. If the date fits, it stays. If not, discard it and draw another.
juego.fechasTexto: A card with just the year fits anywhere in that year. One with month and year fits on any day of that month.
juego.finalTexto: The first player to run out of cards. If several finish in the same round, play one more round with one card each.
juego.estrella: Star memory: place it correctly and you play again.
juego.cuentalo: Tell it: before flipping it, tell the memory. If you miss but the group likes the story, you don’t draw a card.
juego.comodin: Wild card: at the start of the second round, whoever has the most cards takes one. Use it to ask for a clue or swap a card.
juego.enBlanco: Blank cards: when a memory comes up that wasn’t in the deck, write it down with its date and it joins the next game.
juego.modosTexto: Whoever makes the deck knows the dates. These variants make that part of the game.

modos.clasico: The rules above. If the deck maker plays, they start with one extra card.
modos.guardian: The deck maker doesn’t compete. They present each card, rule on “Tell it”, give the wild-card clues and tell the story when it’s flipped. Perfect for a gift: the game is the present.
modos.cooperativo: One memory line for the whole group and 3 lives. Take turns placing and talk it over. The deck maker doesn’t place cards: they can only say “earlier” or “later” once per card. Goal: 15 cards on the line, then beat your record.
modos.duelo: For two. The deck maker starts with 6 cards and doesn’t use wild cards; the other player starts with 4 and can ask for a one-word clue each turn.
modos.generaciones: For families. Make teams that mix ages: older players know the old dates and younger ones the recent ones. Teams take turns and can talk it over.

juego.consejo: Tip: play the first game as Memory Keeper. The second, everyone against the deck.

instrucciones.texto: A 252 × 176 mm sheet that folds into 8 card-sized panels and fits in the box.
instrucciones.plegadoTexto: Fold in half lengthwise (side A outside), then accordion-fold along the three vertical lines. The cover panel ends up on top.
instrucciones.posterTexto: A deck to put your memories in order.
instrucciones.impresion: Print on landscape A4, double-sided flipping on the short edge, at 100%. Cut along the corner marks; the side marks show the folds.
instrucciones.personalizado: With your deck’s title and dedication.
instrucciones.generico: Generic version: make a deck to see your title and dedication.

privacidadPagina.intro: The photos in your deck are personal data and often show children. This is how we handle them:
privacidadPagina.prototipo: Photos are read and stored only in your browser (IndexedDB). They’re never uploaded to a server. The print file is also generated on your device. You can delete everything with “Start another deck”.

real.1: Photos will be stored on servers in the European Union, in private storage, and only viewable through signed links that expire within minutes.
real.2: We’ll ask for your explicit consent before uploading photos.
real.3: We’ll automatically delete original photos and print files 60 days after shipping.
real.4: We don’t run third-party analytics on your images or send them to other services.
real.5: You can ask us at any time to delete your deck and your data.

errores.almacen: Your browser won’t let us save the deck (private mode?). You can carry on, but it will be lost when you close the tab.
